definitions.explanation: A male romantic partner. Used in casual to neutral contexts.

examples.japanese: {彼氏|かれし}と{映画|えいが}を{見|み}に{行|い}った。
examples.english: I went to see a movie with my boyfriend.

examples.japanese: {彼氏|かれし}の{誕生日|たんじょうび}にプレゼントを{買|か}った。
examples.english: I bought a present for my boyfriend's birthday.

examples.japanese: {友達|ともだち}に{彼氏|かれし}を{紹介|しょうかい}したら、みんなに「いい{人|ひと}だね」と{言|い}われた。
examples.english: When I introduced my boyfriend to my friends, everyone said "He seems like a great guy."

examples.japanese: {彼氏|かれし}と{付|つ}き{合|あ}い{始|はじ}めたころは{毎日|まいにち}メッセージを{送|おく}り{合|あ}っていたが、{最近|さいきん}は{週|しゅう}に{一回|いっかい}ぐらいになった。
examples.english: When we first started dating, we would message each other every day, but lately it's about once a week.

notes:
ETYMOLOGY: {彼|かれ} (he) + {氏|し} (honorific suffix). The {氏|し} suffix adds a slight formal/distancing nuance, but the word itself is casual.

CONTRAST:
・{彼氏|かれし} ↔ {彼女|かのじょ} (boyfriend ↔ girlfriend)
・Both are standard casual terms for romantic partners

FORMAL/OTHER EXPRESSIONS:
・{恋人|こいびと} (lover, sweetheart - gender-neutral, slightly formal)
・パートナー (partner - modern, gender-neutral)
・お{付|つ}き{合|あ}いしている{人|ひと} (person I'm dating - polite)
・{交際|こうさい}{相手|あいて} (dating partner - formal)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
・{彼氏|かれし}ができる (to get a boyfriend)
・{彼氏|かれし}と{別|わか}れる (to break up with one's boyfriend)
・{彼氏|かれし}と{付|つ}き{合|あ}う (to date one's boyfriend)
・{彼氏|かれし}がいる (to have a boyfriend)
・{彼氏|かれし}を{紹介|しょうかい}する (to introduce one's boyfriend)

USAGE NOTE:
{彼氏|かれし} is the most common casual term for "boyfriend" in everyday conversation. The term {彼|かれ} alone can also mean "boyfriend" in context, often used when the relationship is already understood.
